note: Proves the snippet path: `children` is a real snippet handed over as a VALUE, and a six-option `role` is above the segmented ceiling so its knob is a SearchablePopover.

states.hover: No prop. `:hover` is not settable from a prop at all — read the plinth's live pseudo-class readout instead.
states.focus-visible: No prop, and a scripted `.focus()` does not match `:focus-visible` in Chromium, so a knob would render nothing and read as a missing focus ring.
states.loading: No `loading` prop, and no way to set `aria-busy` — which the spec requires of a loading control, because Foundry's Font Awesome kills `fa-spin` under reduced motion.
states.invalid: Not applicable: a button holds no value that could be invalid.
states.readonly: Not applicable: a button holds no value that could be read-only.
states.empty: Not applicable: a button renders its children, never a collection.

unknobbed.why: Only reachable with `tag="a"`, and the component deliberately falls back to a button when an anchor has no href — so a driven href would silently change which element renders.
An anchor concern, and navigating away from the lab is not a state worth reaching.
An anchor concern with no visual consequence: it changes the referrer policy and nothing on screen.
An EXTRA class appended to the primitive's own. Driving it would let the lab paint a button the design system does not draw, which is the one thing this page must never do.

note: Proves the write-back: `onChange` declares `writes: "value"`, so pressing the component's OWN plus and minus buttons moves the rendered number. Without it the specimen would log and never move.

states.hover: No prop; see the plinth's pseudo-class readout.
states.focus-visible: No prop; the input's own ring is reachable by tabbing to it on the plinth.
states.loading: No prop. A stepper has no pending state — its edits are synchronous.
states.invalid: No prop. Out-of-range entry is CLAMPED rather than marked invalid, which is a deliberate difference from a validated field.
states.readonly: No prop. `disabled` is the only off state, and the header records that `inputProps.disabled` is the wrong way to reach it.
states.empty: Reachable through `allowUnset`, which makes absence a real value in the field's domain rather than a blank that coerces back to the model.

note: Proves the overlay path: the panel portals into its OWN plinth's `.fabricate-manager` and is clipped by it exactly as the product clips it (issue 1286). The option list is long enough that the panel exceeds a minimum-height plinth, so the clip is observable on purpose rather than by accident, and long enough that the search field is doing something.

states.hover: No prop; see the plinth's pseudo-class readout.
states.focus-visible: No prop. The trigger and every option row take a ring; tab to them on the plinth.
states.loading: No prop. The option list is passed in already resolved, so the component never awaits anything.
states.invalid: No prop. A closed set cannot hold an invalid value; an unmatched `value` simply marks nothing.
states.readonly: No prop. `disabled` and `triggerAriaDisabled` are the two off states and neither is read-only.
states.empty: Reachable by filtering to nothing, which renders `emptyHint` and `emptyDetail` — the component's own empty state.

unknobbed.why: A second, mutually exclusive shape for the same data. Driving both from one panel would let the lab render a combination no call site can produce.
An EXTRA class on the trigger. Driving it would let the harness paint a trigger the design system does not draw.

The search field's accessible name; same reason.

The same state, same route.
